question_text: Identify five ethical traits on which one can plot the performance of a civil servant. Justify their inclusion in the matrix. (Answer in 150 words)
topic: Ethical traits of a civil servant
topics: Ethical traits of a civil servant
keyPointers: Integrity, impartiality, empathy, courage and accountability
A trait must show in a decision
The matrix is useless if it is only a score
Justify each by the harm its absence causes

points.text: A servant's performance can be plotted on traits that show in a file, not on a speech.
Integrity: the decision is not for sale.
Impartiality and accountability: the same rule, and a name on the order.
Empathy and courage: the weak are seen, and a wrong order is refused.
These five belong because the service fails in a predictable way when each is missing.

question_text: Identify ten essential values that are needed to be an effective public servant. Describe the ways and means to prevent non-ethical behaviour in the public servants. (Answer in 150 words)
topic: Values and prevention of unethical conduct
topics: Values and prevention of unethical conduct
subTopics: Values of an effective public servant
keyPointers: Integrity, impartiality, objectivity, dedication, empathy, compassion, tolerance, courage, transparency, accountability
Prevention is a system, not a sermon
A usable clean path and a real consequence
Values without a check do not hold

points.text: An effective servant needs values that survive pressure.
Ten: integrity, impartiality, objectivity, dedication to public service, empathy, compassion, tolerance, courage, transparency and accountability.
Prevention: a clear rule, a disclosure, a rotation, a protected refusal and a punishment that arrives.
Non-ethical behaviour is prevented when the value is backed by a consequence.

question_text: Impact of digital technology as a reliable source of input for rational decision making is a debatable issue. Critically evaluate with suitable example. (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: A dashboard can inform and can mislead
The excluded do not appear in the data
Rational means checking the input
Example: a welfare list that drops the offline poor

points.text: A digital input can make a decision faster and can make a biased one look objective.
Clean administrative data helps a rational choice of where a scheme should go.
A predictive score or an incomplete list hides the person who is offline.
Example: a welfare cutoff that drops the undocumented poor.
Technology is a reliable input only after a human checks who is missing.

question_text: Besides domain knowledge, a public official needs innovativeness and creativity of a high order as well, while resolving ethical dilemmas. Discuss with suitable example. (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: The rule book often offers two bad options
Creativity finds a third that keeps the duty
It is not a trick around the law
Example: a deadline against a safety finding

points.text: Domain knowledge says what the rule is; a dilemma is when two duties pull apart.
Creativity finds a lawful third path: a recorded delay, a partial step, a redesigned process.
Example: a crack that politics wants ignored. The creative duty is a recorded stop and an independent test, not a secret patch.
Innovation here serves the ethic; it does not dodge it.

question_text: What does this quotation mean to you? "Every work has got to pass through hundreds of difficulties before succeeding. Those that persevere will see the light, sooner or later." — Swami Vivekananda (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: Difficulty is the normal path
Perseverance is for a public task
It is not an excuse for a wrong method
The light is the completed duty

points.text: Vivekananda treats the obstacle as the ordinary price of a serious work.
For a servant, a reform will meet a file, a vested interest and a delay.
Perseverance means staying with the lawful aim, not forcing a shortcut.
The line is a call to endurance with a clean means.

question_text: What does this quotation mean to you? "We can never obtain peace in the outer world until and unless we obtain peace within ourselves." — Dalai Lama (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: A disturbed officer spreads the disturbance
Inner peace is not withdrawal
It steadies a decision
Outer order needs people who are not at war with themselves

points.text: The Dalai Lama ties public peace to the state of the person who acts.
An angry or fearful official humiliates, delays or uses force.
Inner peace is a discipline of attention, not an escape from the file.
A calmer servant makes a less violent administration.

question_text: What does this quotation mean to you? "Life doesn't make any sense without interdependence. We need each other, and the sooner we learn that, it is better for us all." — Erik Erikson (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: No public good is a solo act
The servant depends on the citizen and the colleague
Learning it early prevents contempt for the weak
The quote is a civic ethic

points.text: Erikson locates a meaningful life in needing others, not in standing alone.
A scheme works only when the official, the worker and the citizen each do a part.
Contempt for dependence produces a harsh office.
The sooner a servant accepts interdependence, the fairer the service.

question_text: Attitude is an important component that goes as input in the development of human being. How to build a suitable attitude needed for a public servant? (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: Attitude is learnt
Training, example and a consequence shape it
Suitable means the citizen as the principal
It is built, not announced

points.text: A servant's attitude toward the citizen is learnt, so it can be built.
Training on real cases, a senior who models the counter, and a reward that notices the last person.
A posting and a punishment that do not teach contempt.
The suitable attitude is built by example and feedback, not by a circular.

question_text: In case of crisis of conscience does emotional intelligence help to overcome the same without compromising the ethical or moral stand that you are likely to follow? Critically examine. (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: EI names the feeling; conscience names the duty
It can help you hold the stand without an outburst
It can also be used to rationalise a compromise
Helpful, and not a substitute for the stand

points.text: A crisis of conscience is a clash between an order, a fear and a moral stand.
Emotional intelligence helps you see the fear and still speak calmly.
It does not decide the stand; a clever reading of one's feelings can also justify bending.
It helps you keep the stand; it must not be used to dilute it.

question_text: "Refugees should not be turned back to the country where they would face persecution or human right violation." Examine the statement with reference to the ethical dimension being violated by a nation claiming to be democratic with an open society. (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: Sending a person back to persecution breaks a basic duty
A democracy that claims openness is judged here
Security is a real limit, not a blanket
The violation is using the weak as a threat

points.text: The line is the rule that a person is not returned to torture or persecution.
A democracy that turns them back violates the dignity it claims to hold.
A check for a real security risk can be lawful; a blanket pushback is not.
The ethical failure is greatest when an open society closes the door it advertises.

question_text: Should impartial and being non-partisan be considered as indispensable qualities to make a successful civil servant? Discuss with illustrations. (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: The same rule, and no party as the client
Indispensable for a permanent service
Illustration: an election, or a scheme bent toward a party worker
Success without them is a private success

points.text: A permanent service serves successive governments and one public.
Impartiality is the same rule; non-partisanship is refusing a party as the master.
Illustration: an election duty, or a benefit not steered to a worker of the ruling side.
Yes, they are indispensable. A partisan career that looks successful has failed the public.

question_text: An independent and empowered social audit mechanism is an absolute must in every sphere of public service, including judiciary, to ensure performance, accountability and ethical conduct. Elaborate. (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: The user of a service can see whether it happened
Independence is from the office being audited
The judiciary needs a careful form, not a crowd reviewing a judgment
Internal audit marking its own work is not enough

points.text: Social audit lets the people affected check a work, a wage or a service.
It needs an independent facilitator and a record the office cannot quietly rewrite.
For the judiciary the form is transparency of process and a complaint system, not a crowd judging a verdict.
Without an outside check, performance and ethics stay a claim.

question_text: "Integrity is a value that empowers the human being." Justify with suitable illustration. (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: A person who cannot be bought can refuse
Empowerment is the freedom of that refusal
Illustration: an officer who records a wrong order
Integrity is a strength, not only a restraint

points.text: Integrity is doing what you ought to do when it costs.
It empowers because the person is not trapped by a bribe, a fear or a favour already taken.
Illustration: an officer who stops unsafe work and can defend the written note.
The value gives a spine. Its absence hands the person to whoever pays.

question_text: Sunil, a young civil servant posted in a tribal district, acts against an illegal sand-mining mafia linked to some of his own staff and to local musclemen. The mafia threatens him, his wife and mother are stalked, and he is reminded that an officer was killed ten years earlier. (a) Identify the options available to Sunil. (b) Critically evaluate each option. (c) Which option should he adopt and why? (Answer in 250 words)
topic: Illegal sand mining and a threat to the officer
topics: Illegal sand mining and a threat to the officer
keyPointers: Stopping betrays the duty already begun
A lone raid may repeat the earlier killing
The right path is lawful action plus protection
The poor tribal is both a victim and a person the mafia pays

points.text: Options: stop the raids; continue alone; seek a quiet transfer; or continue with a written record, protection for the family, and action against the colluding staff.
Stopping saves the family today and abandons the law and the next officer. A lone raid repeats the risk that killed a predecessor.
The appropriate option is to persist through the system: inform seniors in writing, protect the family, use a legal force, and separate the poor tribal from the mafia.
Courage here is organised, not theatrical.

question_text: You are Vice Principal of a degree college. A flying squad catches two students cheating with help from a senior lecturer close to the management. One student is a local politician's son; the other is the son of a major donor. Management tells you to settle it with the squad at any cost and hints that your promotion to Principal depends on it. Students are protesting for strict action. (a) Discuss the ethical issues. (b) Critically examine your options and state which you will adopt and why. (Answer in 250 words)
topic: Exam cheating and a hinted promotion
topics: Exam cheating and a hinted promotion
keyPointers: The cheat, the lecturer and the cover-up are three wrongs
A promotion that depends on a cover is a bribe in kind
Adopt the lawful report
Tell the protest that the rule, not a slogan, will decide

points.text: Ethical issues: fairness of the exam, misuse of influence, and a personal promotion set against the truth.
Options: hush the squad; punish only the students; or record the facts, support the squad, and refuse the hinted bargain.
Adopt the third. A principalship bought by burying a cheat is not a post worth holding.
The students outside should be told that action will follow the university rule.

question_text: As project manager of an elevated corridor meant to be inaugurated before an election, you find a crack in a pier, likely from poor material, and assess that at least three piers must be rebuilt, delaying the work by four to six months. The chief engineer overrules you, citing the minister, a contractor who is the minister's relative, and your pending promotion. (a) What options do you have? (b) What ethical dilemmas do you face? (c) What professional challenges arise and how should you respond? (d) What follows if the inspection is overlooked? (Answer in 250 words)
topic: A structural crack and a political deadline
topics: A structural crack and a political deadline
keyPointers: A crack in a pier is a future collapse
The deadline and the relative are not engineering facts
Record the stop in writing
Overlooking it transfers the risk to unknown commuters

points.text: Options: obey and continue; resign quietly; or stop the unsafe work, record the assessment, and escalate in writing above the chief engineer.
Dilemmas: safety against a career, and loyalty to a senior against loyalty to the user of the bridge.
The professional pressure is isolation. Respond with a written technical note and a request for an independent test. Do not accept an oral waiver.
Overlooking the crack can mean a later failure, deaths, and a blame that still finds the manager who knew.

question_text: You administer a public hospital during the COVID-19 surge. Patients arrive continuously, and beds, oxygen, staff and cremation capacity are short. (a) What criteria and justification would you use to put clinical and non-clinical staff on duty, knowing the disease is highly infectious? (b) Would the decision be the same if the hospital were private? (Answer in 250 words)
topic: Allocating hospital staff in a pandemic
topics: Allocating hospital staff in a pandemic
subTopics: Duty of care in a shortage
keyPointers: Staff are not an unlimited resource
Criteria: skill, rotation and protection
A public hospital cannot choose only the easy patient
A private hospital owes the same care and the same staff protection

points.text: Criteria: competence for the task, a rotation so no one is exhausted, proper protection, and non-clinical staff on logistics rather than unprotected clinical work.
Justification: the public hospital exists for this surge. Refusing to deploy is abandonment. Deploying without gear is also wrong.
A private hospital owes the same care to the patient in front of it and the same protection to its staff.
It may not dump the severe poor case onto the public system in order to protect profit. Staff safety stays the same; freedom to refuse the poor does not.

question_text: A reputed food company sold in India a product that random tests found did not match its domestic approval, and it also sold rejected export stock in the home market. (a) What should the competent authority do? (b) What can the company do to resolve the crisis and recover reputation? (c) Examine the ethical dilemma. (Answer in 250 words)
subTopics: A double standard in food safety
keyPointers: Rejected export stock must not become the home meal
Stop, recall, penalise
Reputation returns after the product does
The dilemma was a stricter standard for the foreign buyer

points.text: The authority should stop the sale, order a recall, test what remains, suspend the approval and penalise, with prosecution if harm is shown.
The company should admit the variance, recall, compensate, and open the process to an independent audit before it claims the brand back.
The ethical dilemma was a known standard for the export buyer and a weaker product for the domestic one.
Reputation follows the corrected product, not an advertisement.

question_text: Pawan, a state-government officer, is repeatedly humiliated by his senior despite no serious failure in the work. The abuse damages his confidence and then his temper at home. (a) What options does he have? (b) What approach should he take for peace at office and at home? (c) What would you suggest to the boss and to the subordinate? (d) What training would you suggest for officers? (Answer in 250 words)
keyPointers: Humiliation is not a management style
Record, clarify, and use a channel
Do not carry the rage home
Seniors need training in conduct

points.text: Options: endure; retaliate; seek a transfer; or record the incidents, ask for a calm clarification, and use the grievance channel if it continues.
Separate work feedback from insult. Do not punish the family for the office. A colleague or a counsellor can witness the pattern.
To the boss: criticise in private and on the work. To Pawan: do not answer abuse with abuse.
Training: a workplace code, emotional intelligence for supervising officers, and a redress that juniors trust.
